models_evaluated: Seven versions of an EHR-embedded AI agent for clinicians

links.outcome: Whether clinician-authored case-specific rubrics discriminate high- from low-quality AI outputs, and stability of scoring
links.effect: Median score gap between preferred and rejected outputs was 82.9%, with median scoring range of 0.00%. Clinician-LLM ranking agreement (tau 0.42-0.46) matched or exceeded clinician-clinician agreement (tau 0.38-0.43).
links.quote: Clinician-authored rubrics discriminated effectively between high- and low-quality outputs (median score gap: 82.9%) with high scoring stability (median range: 0.00%).

unlisted_practices: Using LLM-generated case-specific rubrics as a low-cost (~1,000x cheaper) substitute for per-instance expert review in iterative clinical AI evaluation
Validating each rubric by confirming an LLM scoring agent scores clinician-preferred outputs above rejected ones
Managing ceiling compression when measuring inter-rater agreement in AI evaluation

screen.reason: The study validates a scalable evaluation methodology (clinician- and LLM-authored case-specific rubrics with an LLM scoring agent) to support continuous testing and iterative deployment of clinical documentation AI agents.

primary.practice: case-specific rubrics and automated LLM-based evaluation for clinical AI monitoring
